- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overcorrect downward; if below, overcorrects upward — apply opposite bias correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 2–4 days ahead to align with sentiment direction.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
